user_prompt: What is the effect of manual therapy (manipulation, mobilisation, soft-tissue techniques), prescribed exercise, or a combination of the two, compared with minimal or no intervention (wait-and-see, advice only, placebo or sham, usual GP care), on pain intensity in adults with lateral elbow pain (tennis elbow, lateral epicondylalgia), measured at the end of the intervention period?  Effect measure: pool as a mean difference (MD) on a 0 to 10 pain scale using a random-effects model. MD < 0 means less pain with the active treatment (favours the treatment). Convert 0 to 100 mm visual analogue scale values to 0 to 10 by dividing means and SDs by 10.  Outcome: mean pain intensity (for example pain at rest, on activity or on maximum grip; prefer the trial's primary pain measure) at the end of the intervention period, extracted as the mean, SD and number of participants per arm. - Use the first assessment at the end of treatment (typically 6 to 8 weeks). Do not use later follow-up assessments. - Use end-of-intervention means and SDs when they are reported. If only the change from baseline is given (mean change and SD of change), use those for both arms and state that change scores were used. If only an adjusted between-group difference with a confidence interval (95% or 99%) is reported, use that: take the SE from the interval (95%: width ÷ 3.92; 99%: width ÷ 5.15) and state that an adjusted difference was used. Do not mix end values and change scores within a trial. - If the number analysed per arm is not stated for the pain outcome, use the number randomised to each arm (or the arm sizes in the flow diagram) and state this. Do not leave group sizes blank. - If variability is reported as SE or SEM, convert to SD = SE × √n. Check table footnotes for whether "±" is SD or SE. - If the paper gives data only in a figure, leave the trial out and say so. - Orient the difference as treatment minus control, and invert it if the paper reports control minus treatment. - A control that receives only advice, stretching, usual care or a placebo or sham counts as minimal intervention. Exclude trials whose control group receives another active manual therapy or exercise programme, or an injection or drug. - Multi-arm trials: include each eligible active arm (manual therapy, exercise, or both) against the shared minimal-intervention group, splitting the control group's n equally across the comparisons; or combine the active arms into one group and use the control once, and state the choice. - Include only randomised controlled trials in adults with lateral elbow pain.  Do not pool disability, grip strength, quality of life, treatment success, withdrawals or adverse events.
